rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Module prose carrying a Session widget or a {{prompt:}} fence is an exercise that has not been extracted
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule guards: a `##`-cut deck renders an unextracted multi-beat procedure as one crammed slide with individual moves having nothing to land on. Present but weak here: grep -n "^##\|{{prompt:" plan-mode-done-right.md shows 'Save the rule if it earned itself' (line 41) is ONE `##` heading holding two {{prompt:}} fences (lines 45, 49) plus two body callouts and a closing lecture link - the literal mechanical tell fires. But the identical shape (2 prompts under one shared `##` heading, no extraction) already ships unflagged in the same corpus: earn-the-trust.md 'Clear the session' (grep -n "^##\|{{prompt:" earn-the-trust.md, lines 69/73/79) carries 2 prompts under one heading and has not been extracted either, and this module's own Transitions line (120) bills the section as a 3-min 'soft-compound' close-ritual, not a full exercise-scale procedure (M4's extracted precedent had 4 prompts; M5's had a Session widget plus a prompt). The rule as worded has no size/beat-count threshold, so it fires on a much smaller, arguably-intentional closing beat than the M4/M5 cases that produced it.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Rule question for the maintainer, not a fix to apply: does §52c's extraction requirement carry an implicit size/beat-count floor (a short 2-prompt closing-ritual under one heading vs. the 4-prompt/Session-widget scale of the M4/M5 precedent it was written from)? If short closing rituals are meant to be exempt, word that threshold into §52c so the same shape in earn-the-trust.md's 'Clear the session' section reads consistently against it.
